business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P4 (10-Q MD&A)
business_model.claim: RLJ Lodging Trust is a Maryland REIT that owns premium-branded, focused-service and compact full-service hotels and earns revenue by selling room stays, food and beverage, and ancillary services to guests.
quotes: We are a self-advised and self-administered Maryland real estate investment trust that owns primarily premium-branded, rooms-oriented, high-margin, focused-service and compact full-service hotels located within heart of demand locations.

business_model.claim: The company's customers are predominantly transient business and leisure travelers, supplemented by group bookings (10+ rooms) and a smaller extended-stay segment (5+ nights).
quotes: The majority of our customers are transient in nature. Transient business typically represents individual business or leisure travelers.
Group business is typically defined as a minimum of 10 guestrooms booked together as part of the same piece of business.
Extended-stay customers are generally defined as those staying five nights or longer.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A); revenue line items confirmed in F2 (10-Q income statement)
business_model.claim: Total revenues comprise three streams: room revenue (approximately 81.0% of total in 2025), food and beverage revenue, and other revenue (parking, resort fees, gift shop, guest service fees).
quotes: Room revenue comprised approximately 81.0% of our total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025
Other revenue — Occupancy and the nature of the hotel property are the main drivers of other ancillary revenue, such as parking fees, resort fees, gift shop sales and other guest service fees.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1, Organizational Structure)
business_model.claim: The company operates through a UPREIT structure: the Operating Partnership owns the hotels, leases them to TRS subsidiaries, and the TRSs engage independent third-party managers who collect revenue and pay operating costs.
quotes: We conduct our business through a traditional umbrella partnership real estate investment trust ("UPREIT") structure in which our assets are owned and our business activities are undertaken by the Operating Partnership and its subsidiaries.

The independent managers operate the hotels, collect hotel operating revenue, pay operating expenses (including the independent managers' management fees) on behalf of the TRSs pursuant to the relevant hotel management agreement.

business_model.basis: stated in P4 (10-Q MD&A) and P1 (10-K Item 1, Our Hotels)
business_model.claim: As of June 30, 2026 the portfolio comprised 92 hotel properties with approximately 20,600 rooms in 23 states and the District of Columbia, with 89.3% of properties affiliated with Marriott, Hilton, or Hyatt brands.
quotes: As of June 30, 2026, we owned 92 hotel properties with approximately 20,600 rooms, located in 23 states and the District of Columbia.
approximately 89.3% of our hotel properties operating under existing relationships with Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A, Key Indicators) and P4 (10-Q MD&A); Q3 2026 figures from P6
business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by two primary variables: Occupancy (rooms sold / rooms available) and Average Daily Rate (room revenue / rooms sold); their product is RevPAR.
quotes: RevPAR is the product of ADR and Occupancy.
Occupancy represents the total number of hotel rooms sold in a given period divided by the total number of rooms available.
ADR represents the total hotel room revenues divided by the total number of rooms sold in a given period.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A, Principal Factors Affecting Our Results of Operations)
business_model.claim: Operating costs are predominantly variable with Occupancy (labor, supplies, utilities), while ADR increases mainly add management and franchise fees that are computed as a percentage of revenue.
quotes: Most categories of variable operating expenses, including labor costs, fluctuate with changes in Occupancy.
A base management fee is computed as a percentage of gross hotel revenues.
A franchise fee is computed as a percentage of room revenue, plus an additional percentage of room revenue for marketing, central reservation systems and other franchisor costs.

business_model.claim: The lodging business is seasonal, with northeastern properties experiencing lower revenues in winter (Dec–Mar) and Florida properties peaking in Jan–Apr, causing quarterly revenue fluctuations.
quotes: The lodging industry is seasonal in nature, which can cause quarterly fluctuations in our revenues. For example, our hotels in the northeastern metropolitan areas experience lower revenues and profits during the winter months of December through March, while our hotels in Florida generally have higher revenues in the months of January through April.
